headline: Software Surge and Financials Lead Into a Geopolitics-Heavy Thursday
body_html:
Wall Street gets Thursday's session under way with diplomacy and Middle East shipping risks crowding the news flow, and with Wednesday's strong close as the backdrop. Of the 664 stocks we track, 413 rose and 246 fell on Wednesday. Financials led the sectors with a gain of 3.16%, followed by Consumer at 2.39%, Software at 1.48% and Homebuilders at 1.46%.

Cybersecurity and cloud names did the heavy lifting. Tenable jumped 15.75%, Qualys 12.92%, Netskope 12.73%, Fastly 12.58% and Okta 12.07%, while Vital Farms gained 13.61%. The weak spots were Energy, down 1.83%, and gold miners, with DRDGOLD off 7.03% and Agnico Eagle off 6.44%. Baytex Energy lost 6.19%, and Applied Optoelectronics fell 9.8%.

At the open, watch whether the software rebound holds after such a sharp one-day move, and whether Energy steadies. Oil headlines remain jumpy, with shipping attacks, a tighter Iran blockade and a missile threat toward Riyadh all in play. Trump's Asia tour diplomacy is another swing factor. Pre-market prices are thin and say little yet, so the first hour of trading will tell more.

briefs.headline: Kremlin Says Ukraine Dominated Putin Talks
briefs.body: Russian officials said Ukraine was the central subject when Vladimir Putin met Donald Trump during the American president's Asia swing. Trump had earlier told Xi Jinping that Washington and Beijing could help bring the war to a close. Traders will look for any hint of follow-through.

briefs.headline: Oil Holds Steady as Shipping Risks Offset Supply Glut
briefs.body: Crude has largely stood still as attacks on Middle East shipping counterbalance forecasts of ample supply. Energy shares were the weakest sector in Wednesday's session, down 1.83%. The open will show whether the group stabilizes or the slide extends.

briefs.headline: Washington Tightens Iran Blockade at Sea
briefs.body: A new advisory shows US authorities adding limits on ship-to-ship oil transfers as part of the blockade on Iran. Such curbs can complicate how barrels move to buyers. Energy traders will be watching for any effect on shipping and pricing.

briefs.headline: South Korea Hits Export Milestone on AI Chip Demand
briefs.body: South Korea has become only the fourth nation to reach a trillion dollars of annual exports, with the surge in artificial-intelligence chips cited as a driver. Semiconductor stocks in our universe were nearly flat Wednesday, down 0.04%, leaving the sector a place to watch.

briefs.headline: EU Agrees to Push Back Methane Rules by Two Years
briefs.body: European governments and Parliament have settled on a two-year delay to the bloc's methane regulation. The postponement gives energy importers and suppliers more time to prepare. It also eases a compliance pressure point for the gas and oil industry.

briefs.headline: Orlen and QatarEnergy Reportedly Discuss New LNG Deal
briefs.body: Poland's Orlen and QatarEnergy are said to be in talks on a fresh liquefied natural gas agreement, sources told Reuters, only days after an earlier contract was terminated. The development highlights how quickly gas supply arrangements are being reshuffled across Europe.
